big_idea: Every object has MEASURABLE ATTRIBUTES: length, area, mass, capacity.
learning_intention: We are learning to name measurable attributes.
student_learning_goal: I can name measurable attributes of objects.
success_criteria: I can name LENGTH, AREA, MASS, CAPACITY.
I can pick the right attribute for an object.
I can explain why I chose that attribute.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Roo and Cal — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
Lesson 1 attribute tracker — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: Roo: This pencil has LENGTH. This book has AREA. This rock has MASS. This cup has CAPACITY! Roo opens: 'Measure it!' Class: 'Match it!' Cal: 'Mark the day!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Roo and Cal puppets. 'Friends — I'm Roo the Ruler Rabbit. Today we name MEASURABLE ATTRIBUTES of objects.'

Introduce vocabulary. Write ATTRIBUTE, LENGTH, AREA, MASS, CAPACITY on chart. 'Attribute = a way to describe an object. Length = how long. Area = how much flat space. Mass = how heavy. Capacity = how much it holds.'

Demonstrate. Hold up a pencil. 'What attribute? LENGTH — we measure how long.' Hold up a book. 'AREA — we measure the cover space.' Hold up a rock. 'MASS — we measure how heavy.' Hold up a cup. 'CAPACITY — we measure how much it holds.'

More examples:
- Ruler: length
- Carpet: area
- Backpack: mass + capacity
- Door: length (height) + area

'Roo says — most objects have MORE THAN ONE attribute.'

'Today we name attributes for lots of objects.'

steps.instruction: Whole group: name attributes for 6 classroom objects.
Three stations. Station A: Sort 16 attribute cards into the 4 categories. Station B: Pick an object and list its attributes. Station C: Multi-attribute hunt — find 5 objects with 2+ attributes.
Stretch challenge at Station C: name 5 attributes for one object (length, area, mass, capacity, plus colour or shape).
Discuss attribute choice. 'Some attributes apply to all objects (length). Some only to specific (capacity = container only).'
steps.teacher_prompt: Show: a rock has mass but not capacity.

steps.instruction: Circulate to record diagnostic evidence on the attribute tracker.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each pair. Ask 'What's the attribute?' Mark the tracker.

steps.instruction: STRATEGY COMPARE at Station C: two pairs share how they decided which attribute to name for an AMBIGUOUS object (backpack — mass? capacity? both?). Class compares reasoning. Cite Sarama & Clements 2009 attribute trajectory: precise naming is the prerequisite for comparison and ordering.
steps.teacher_prompt: Roo: 'A backpack has MASS (it's heavy when full) AND CAPACITY (it holds your books). The math word matters — pick the one you can MEASURE.'

differentiation.for_emerging: Stay at Station A. Just sort 8 cards into 2 categories.
differentiation.for_extending: Stretch at Station C: 5 attributes per object.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Children carry objects around the room and name attributes aloud.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: names 4 attributes; picks the right one; explains why.

discussion_prompts: Can one object have many attributes?
Roo's preview: tomorrow we'll COMPARE lengths and areas (Lesson 2 — E2.1). Look at your sticky — would TWO of those things compare by the same attribute, or different ones?
consolidation.exit_routine: Roo's unit refrain — Roo calls 'Measure it!' Class chants 'Match it!' Cal echoes 'Mark the day!' Repeat 3x. Each child writes one object + the attribute they would measure on a sticky.

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 1 surfaces children who already use measurement vocabulary.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child confuses MASS and CAPACITY — repairing the mass-capacity mix-up at Grade 1
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
When children pick up a measurable object and are asked 'what can you measure?', the dominant Grade-1 trap is attribute confusion: child says 'big' (vague), or names mass for a hollow container when they meant capacity, or names capacity for solids. Sarama & Clements (2009, 'Early Childhood Mathematics Education Research: Learning Trajectories for Young Children') place attribute discrimination as the foundation of all later measurement reasoning — without it, comparison (Lesson 2-3) and ordering (Lesson 4-5) have nothing to compare or order.

Today's task is precise attribute naming: LENGTH, AREA, MASS, CAPACITY. Tomorrow Lesson 2 compares lengths and areas; Day 3 compares mass and capacity; Day 4 introduces calendar; Day 5 integrates.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair is at Station B. Child holds a cup. Says 'this cup's attribute is MASS' when asked about how much it can hold.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'You said MASS. Roo asks — when you HOLD water in this cup, what attribute is that?'

Walk through. 'CAPACITY = how much it HOLDS. MASS = how HEAVY it is. They're different.'

Generalise. 'Roo says — when in doubt, ASK "is this about HOLDING (capacity) or WEIGHT (mass)?"'

Now practice. 'A rock — has it got CAPACITY?' (No.) 'A cup of water — has it got CAPACITY?' (Yes.)

If still mixed: provide a sorting card. 'CAPACITY only applies to CONTAINERS.'

Long-term recovery: every attribute identification names the test.
common_misconceptions: Capacity = mass. (Repair: capacity is about HOLDING, mass is about WEIGHT.)
All objects have all 4 attributes. (Repair: capacity only for containers.)
Length and area are the same. (Repair: length is 1D, area is 2D.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child names mass for ANY container (full or empty): contrast a full cup vs empty cup. Same container, different mass; child says 'mass changes when you fill it; capacity stays the same.'
DIAGNOSTIC B — child applies capacity to solids (a brick has 'capacity'): sort objects into two trays — CONTAINERS (have capacity) vs SOLIDS (no inside, no capacity). Child re-categorises.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child cannot articulate any attribute: model 4 questions on one object — How LONG? How much AREA? How heavy (MASS)? How much fits inside (CAPACITY)? Child repeats with a second object.

parts_outline.task: Match 6 objects to their attribute (length / area / mass / capacity).
Pick one object. List 2 attributes it has.
Find 3 objects in your home. Name an attribute for each.
